newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn mixed, nearbys up on demand ideas.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn mixed, nearbys up on demand ideas.

text.p: CBOT corn futures were mixed at midsession with nearbys up on ideas of improving export and domestic demand but new crop was down on ideas U.S. corn plantings will increase, traders said.

Floor sources pointed to news South Korea bought 105,000 tonnes U.S. corn on Monday. They also cited ideas U.S. feed usage would increase as pork producers raced to meet demand left by Taiwan's pork export ban.
Taiwan on Wednesday ordered the slaughter of all hogs, even healthy ones, at farms affected by an outbreak of foot and mouth disease.

The council said more than one million hogs would be destroyed. It said the fast-moving foot-and-mouth epidemic had spread to 716 pig breeding centers by Wednesday, almost double the 357 reported on Monday.

New crop months were pressured by ideas 1997 corn plantings would increase. A Reuter survey of analysts produced an average estimate of 80.92 million acres of corn, up from 79.49 million last year. Stocks were estimated by analysts at 4.565 billion bushels, well above last year's 3.8 billion.
At 1123 CST, corn was up 1-1/4 to down 1-1/4 cents per bushel with May up 1-1/4 at $3.03-1/2.
